title: AI Media and Visual Repository
answer: Keynotes, conference talks, tutorials, podcasts with transcripts, and a diagram and image library.

reading.body:
The AI media repository is a curated index of 18 items across video, podcasts, and diagrams, not a live feed or a ranking.

The three sections split by format rather than by topic. Video covers vendor keynotes where model and hardware announcements land, conference talks, university lecture series, and onboarding explainers. Podcasts are tracked by host, focus, and whether transcripts exist. The image library covers architecture diagrams, illustrated walkthroughs, and browser-based model explorers.

For AI specifically, the useful signal is where primary announcements surface. Vendor keynotes are named as the place model and hardware announcements land, which ties this media layer back to compute and hardware news rather than to research alone. Transcript availability is tracked for podcasts, which matters because text is what can be searched, quoted, and fed into other systems.

What the data does not contain is any count of episodes, views, downloads, or publication dates. The counts of 7, 6, and 5 describe catalog entries, not activity or popularity. Nothing here measures whether any of these sources is current, accurate, or widely used.
